task_description:
# Quest Tracking System with Godot 4 Custom Resources

## Background
Design a data-driven quest tracking system for a Godot 4 game using custom `Resource` types. The system must support multiple quests organized into a prerequisite chain, multi-step objectives that can be incrementally progressed, and rewards delivered when a quest is completed.

## Requirements
- A custom `Resource` class `QuestObjective` with serializable progress data.
- A custom `Resource` class `Quest` aggregating objectives, prerequisites, and rewards.
- Three concrete `.tres` quest assets that form a prerequisite chain (`quest_a` -> `quest_b` -> `quest_c`).
- An autoloaded `QuestManager` singleton that manages quest registration, prerequisite checks, starting quests, progress reporting, and completion, and that emits signals consumers can subscribe to.

## Implementation Hints
- Use `class_name` and `extends Resource` so that the custom Resources can be instantiated in the inspector and saved as `.tres`.
- Use `@export` on every field that must be authored in the inspector and serialized; for typed arrays of custom resources use the `Array[Type]` syntax.
- Register the manager via `project.godot`'s `[autoload]` section so that it is available globally.
- Prefer `StringName` for stable identifiers; convert raw strings using the `&"..."` literal when comparing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Project path: /home/user/quest_project
- The project must run with the headless Godot binary `godot` already installed in the environment.
- Resource scripts:
  - `scripts/QuestObjective.gd` with `class_name QuestObjective`, `extends Resource`, exported fields `description: String`, `target_count: int`, `current_count: int` (default 0), and an `is_complete() -> bool` method.
  - `scripts/Quest.gd` with `class_name Quest`, `extends Resource`, exported fields `id: StringName`, `title: String`, `description: String`, `objectives: Array[QuestObjective]`, `prerequisite_quest_ids: Array[StringName]`, `reward_gold: int`, `reward_items: Array[StringName]`, methods `is_complete() -> bool` and `get_progress() -> float` (returning a value in `[0.0, 1.0]`).
- Quest assets under `resources/quests/`: `quest_a.tres`, `quest_b.tres`, `quest_c.tres`; each loadable via `load("res://resources/quests/<id>.tres")` and exposing the chain `quest_b.prerequisite_quest_ids == [&"quest_a"]` and `quest_c.prerequisite_quest_ids == [&"quest_b"]`.
- Autoload `QuestManager` declared in `project.godot` pointing to `res://autoloads/QuestManager.gd`, exposing:
  - `register_quest(quest: Quest) -> void`
  - `can_start(quest_id: StringName) -> bool` (true only if every prerequisite is in the completed set)
  - `start_quest(quest_id: StringName) -> bool` (returns false and does not start if prerequisites are unmet; emits `quest_started(id)`)
  - `report_progress(objective_key: StringName, amount: int = 1) -> void` (for each active quest, increments `current_count` of every objective whose `description` matches `objective_key`, capped at `target_count`; emits `quest_progress(id, progress)` once per affected quest where `progress` is the value returned by `Quest.get_progress()`)
  - `complete_quest(quest_id: StringName) -> bool` (returns false if not all objectives complete; on success marks the quest in `completed_ids` and emits `quest_completed(id, reward_gold, reward_items)`)
  - Signals: `quest_started(id)`, `quest_progress(id, progress)`, `quest_completed(id, reward_gold, reward_items)`.
- Verification will be performed by loading the project headlessly with `godot --headless --path /home/user/quest_project` and executing test harness scripts injected into the project that import the manager and these resources directly.

# Verification Plan

## Setup
- The Godot project lives at `/home/user/quest_project`.
- The headless Godot 4 binary is available as `godot` on `PATH`.
- The verifier copies a small test harness `.gd`/`.tscn` into the project, then runs `godot --headless --path /home/user/quest_project res://__verify__/run.tscn` and parses JSON results emitted to stdout.

## Verification Steps
1. Confirm `scripts/QuestObjective.gd` declares `class_name QuestObjective`, `extends Resource`, and exports `description: String`, `target_count: int`, `current_count: int`.
2. Confirm `scripts/Quest.gd` declares `class_name Quest`, `extends Resource`, and exports `id: StringName`, `title: String`, `description: String`, `objectives: Array[QuestObjective]`, `prerequisite_quest_ids: Array[StringName]`, `reward_gold: int`, `reward_items: Array[StringName]`.
3. Load `res://resources/quests/quest_a.tres`, `quest_b.tres`, `quest_c.tres`; assert `quest_a.id == &"quest_a"`, `quest_b.prerequisite_quest_ids == [&"quest_a"]`, `quest_c.prerequisite_quest_ids == [&"quest_b"]`, and each quest has at least one `QuestObjective`.
4. Verify `QuestManager` is configured as an autoload in `project.godot`.
5. From the harness: register all three quests, then assert `QuestManager.can_start(&"quest_a") == true` and `QuestManager.can_start(&"quest_b") == false`.
6. Call `QuestManager.start_quest(&"quest_a")` and confirm the `quest_started` signal fires with argument `&"quest_a"`.
7. Call `QuestManager.report_progress` repeatedly with objective keys matching `quest_a`'s objectives until each `current_count == target_count`; confirm `current_count` never exceeds `target_count` and that `quest_progress` is emitted on each call. Verify `QuestManager.get_progress` style: call `quest_a.get_progress()` and assert the returned value equals `1.0` once all objectives are complete and is `0.0` before any progress.
8. Call `QuestManager.complete_quest(&"quest_a")`; verify it returns `true`, that `quest_completed` is emitted with `(&"quest_a", quest_a.reward_gold, quest_a.reward_items)`, and that subsequently `QuestManager.can_start(&"quest_b") == true`.
9. Call `QuestManager.complete_quest(&"quest_b")` before any progress and assert it returns `false` and emits no `quest_completed` signal.
10. The harness writes JSON lines `RESULT: {"name": ..., "ok": true|false, "detail": ...}` to stdout; the verifier asserts every result has `ok == true`.
